abstract: High-frequency reconstruction in bandwidth extension (BWE) depends on joined interactions among nonlinear spectral, temporal, and perceptual features; assigning a separate discriminator to each such feature may be redundant and may fail to model their joint interactions. We introduce quantum-informed generative model Q-BWE, where we design a five-qubit Quantum Chaos Discriminator (QCD) instead of using separate discriminator for every features, for modeling nonlinear joined-feature interactions efficiently. Our QCD explores a compact five-qubit quantum-inspired inductive bias based on data re-uploading circuit, trainable controlled NOT (CNOT) rotations, quantum entangling gates, and statevector measurement map. Five features for five qubits are selected from a 26-dimensional speech-dynamics bank and are encoded by a two-layer statevector circuit, producing 31 measurements map of local behavior, correlations, mixedness, and Born entropy. QCD guides a Lattice-ConformerNeXt generator with FiLM conditioning and a cosine-masked residual pathway, while delayed-reward Thompson sampling adaptively controls its contribution. The circuit is simulated on classical hardware. Overall, Q-BWE achieves competitive performance on VCTK English, and MLS French datasets in multilingual and multi speaker setups under clean and noisy conditions across a broad set of evaluation metrics with approximately 1.72x fewer parameters (33.5M vs. 19.4M) compared to recent CIS-BWE baseline published in ACL.

oneSentenceThesis: Q-BWE 要从窄带语音恢复缺失高频，用五量子比特的量子混沌判别器一次建模多特征联合分布，并以 FiLM 条件与升余弦掩膜约束生成器，在 VCTK 与 MLS 上以约一半参数达到可比的过平滑与感知质量，但结论只在原文的单种子与多指标折中条件下成立。
originalTitle: Q-BWE: Quantum Chaos-Informed Speech Bandwidth Extension
